working.title: Loaded the need figures
working.detail: Residents of every age: 91,020 people in 8 local authorities in England and Wales. From TS008 - Sex (NM_2028_1). A copy kept on this machine was used, so nothing was fetched.

working.title: Loaded the centre of each local authority
working.detail: 8 local authorities in England and Wales, each with the latitude and longitude the ONS publishes for it. A copy kept on this machine was used, so nothing was fetched.

working.title: Read the site positions
working.detail: 2 rows. 0 had no latitude or longitude, or one that is not a number of degrees, and were left out.

working.title: Measured the distance to the nearest site
working.detail: Area: England and Wales. No catchment was given, so every local authority in England and Wales is compared. For each of its 8 local authorities, the straight-line distance from its centre to the nearest of your 2 sites was measured, to the nearest kilometre. A site outside the area still counts as the nearest when it is. A local authority is within reach when that distance is 10 km or less.

working.title: Listed the places far from a site
working.detail: The 5 local authorities more than 10 km from a site were put in order of people, most first. The first 5 are listed.

checks.question: Is the address of every site public?
checks.why: The distances from several local authorities can show roughly where a site is. Do not share the result if a site's address is confidential, such as a refuge.

checks.question: Does the data list every site people can use today?
checks.why: A site left out makes the places near it look far from help. A site that has closed does the opposite.

checks.question: Is straight-line distance a fair guide where you work?
checks.why: A river, a hill or a poor bus service can make a near site hard to reach. The analysis cannot see them.

checks.question: Are these the people your sites are for: Residents of every age?
checks.why: Distance matters for the people who would use a site. Change the 'need' option if another measure fits better.

checks.question: Is this the area you could serve: England and Wales?
checks.why: A place you could never reach is not a gap. Name the area with the 'catchment' option.

caveats: Distance is in a straight line. Roads, rivers, hills and public transport can make a short distance a long journey.
Distance is measured from the centre of each local authority, not from where each person lives. In a large local authority many people are much nearer or much farther than the figure says.
The figures say how far people are from a site. They do not say how far the people you see travel, or whether anyone far away needs you.
The residents are everyone counted on census day, 21 March 2021, of every age. Not all of them need what you offer.

notes: This analysis is about sites, not about people, so it hides no count.
The result holds distances and public counts for local authorities. It names no site and repeats no postcode or position.
Distances are given to the nearest kilometre. Even so, the distances from several local authorities can show roughly where a site is. Do not share the result if a site's address is confidential.
The need figures are public counts and are shown in full.

charts.title: Distance to your nearest site from the places listed

answer: Counting each person at the centre of their local authority, residents are 80.8 km from your nearest site on average, and 40.7% are within 10 km of one. Of the places farther away, a new site would reach most residents in Birmingham.
